prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: waiting for the loss adjuster. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the loss adjuster is already booked, I keep the member updated with the expected visit window and explain that we cannot progress reserve or liability decisions beyond the evidence we have until their report lands."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there is obvious active damage, I do not wait for the adjuster to confirm immediate mitigation steps; I authorise drying, board-up or temporary repairs within delegated authority so the claim does not worsen."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the adjuster delay is caused by weather or a surge in losses, I set a clear next contact date rather than leaving the case open-ended, because members cope better when they know when they will hear from us again."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the loss is straightforward and the photos, receipts and notes are enough, I prefer to continue triage rather than hold the file for an adjuster just because one was requested initially."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the adjuster is needed to confirm cause or scope, I keep the claim moving by collecting extra evidence in the meantime, such as date-stamped photos, meter readings, or garage invoices, so the report can be actioned quickly."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member is waiting for an adjuster visit after a water leak, I remind myself to check whether temporary accommodation or alternative transport needs reviewing separately, because those decisions need not always wait for the site report."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the adjuster appointment has slipped more than once, I prefer to escalate for a revised booking or a second opinion rather than simply re-chasing, as repeated silence erodes confidence very quickly."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the adjuster report is likely to affect settlement, I avoid promising a final figure before it arrives and instead explain the possible outcomes, so the member understands why the claim is still under assessment."},{"type":"observation","content":"When waiting becomes the main issue, I find it useful to summarise the whole claim timeline in one note, because it helps the next handler see what is pending, what has been authorised, and what still needs evidence."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the delay is outside the member's control, I prefer a tone that acknowledges the inconvenience plainly and without jargon, since a simple apology and a practical next step usually does more good than a long explanation."}]}
